executiveSummary: GM0826 passes the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract. Its CBS/PDOK 2025 identity, 58,380-person municipality control, 44 neighbourhoods in fourteen districts, four BAG places, sixteen BRT settlements, 52 scheduled-transit stop areas and eight domestic NWB logical links are coherent; rounded neighbourhood rows sum to 58,370, only ten below the separately published control (-0.017%). Release is nevertheless correction-required. Oosterhout has genuine water-safety pathways around the Wilhelminakanaal, Amertak, Donge, Mark-regional control system and low/outside-dike Weststad, yet the river preset reports exactly 1.862192 inundation stress from T+12 through T+72, 29,517 affected resident-equivalents at T+24 and 2,421,930.234 deprived person-hours at T+72 without selecting an Amer/Donge/Mark boundary, one of two contained LIWO primary candidates, defence/control state, connected footprint, arrival or recession. Direct open-coast water is correctly zero and should remain suppressed in that narrow source scope, not become an all-clear for delta backwater, canal, polder, sewer, groundwater or pluvial mechanisms. The pluvial preset reports 0.253573 at T+12/T+24 and Drainage availability 0.594860 at T+24 without using the municipality's detailed Oosterheide/Centrum 70 mm studies, sewer, groundwater, pump or receiving-water state. Seven unrelated active hazards reuse nearly the same population-led leading neighbourhoods. A controlled T+24 fire at the official Bosgebied Dorst centre produces direct flame 0.612618, smoke 0.609186 and 17,408 affected, but the containing neighbourhood ranks 32/44 by affected residents while Centrum leads. Static residents badly understate industrial/transient exposure: Weststad-Zuid has zero residents but 135 businesses and 122 non-residential buildings, while the municipality describes Weststad as a roughly 350 ha road/water/rail logistics area. The graph contains A27/A59/N629/N282/N631 but does not consume current/scheduled Rijkswaterstaat restrictions, cross-boundary care access or incident-time road/transit state. Public context identifies 108 water/wastewater objects, seven fresh Waterinfo observations, one Enexis planning sample, 90 antennas and 37 education locations, but none establishes complete live topology, flow, backup, staffing or restoration. Unknown, NoData, candidate catalogues, plans, registers, schedules and timestamped zero discharge must never become zero risk, safe, open or operational.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0826 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place, settlement and safety-region context
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated snapshots retrieved 31 August–2 September 2026
supports: Annual CBS/PDOK inputs identify GM0826 as Oosterhout in Noord-Brabant and safety region Midden- en West-Brabant and report 58,380 residents, density 817/km², 23.8% aged 65 or older and 8,989 one-person households; the generated centre [4.858273351696914,51.62967387967753] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Forty-four neighbourhood rows in fourteen districts sum to 58,370 residents, ten below the separately rounded municipality control (-0.017%); households sum to 26,505 and independently rounded age-65-plus rows to 13,915. Allocation reconciles to the municipality control without rewriting published rows.

BAG supplies Den Hout, Dorst, Oosteind and Oosterhout; BRT supplies sixteen source-labelled settlements: four woonkernen, ten buurtschappen, one deelkern and one gehucht. No generated BAG place centre falls outside the generalized municipal boundary.

All 36 CBS fields are exposed. District heating and public charging are null in all 44 rows, cars per household in eight and eleven other fields in four rows; null/suppression remains NoData. CBS/PDOK is CC BY 4.0 and BAG is Public Domain Mark 1.0.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Wilhelminakanaal–Amertak–Donge water-safety task and Oosterhout outside-dike context
evidenceSources.edition: Current WAD project page; municipality environmental vision inspected 3 September 2026
supports: The water board identifies a primary water-safety task around the Wilhelminakanaal, Amertak and Donge in Geertruidenberg, Drimmelen and Oosterhout. Strengthening or an alternative system solution is required by 2050, with a system choice planned for 2027/2028.

The municipal environmental vision at https://www.oosterhout.nl/fileadmin/user_upload/Omgevingsvisie_Oosterhout.pdf identifies Weststad and some residential areas outside the dikes, discusses flood risk and an Amer-side system measure. It is strategic context, not an incident-time defence state or inundation forecast.
The two contained LIWO primary candidate points are both named Wilhelminakanaal and reference dike rings 35 and 37. Eligibility does not select a breach, footprint or probability.

Future-standard non-compliance and an early design/exploration programme do not mean current failure. No public incident-time defence/structure-state feed or blanket machine-reuse licence was identified on the cited planning pages.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — LIWO 2025.1.6 candidates and current Oosterhout/Marksluis Waterinfo observations
evidenceSources.edition: LIWO application 2025.1.6; WFS and Waterinfo deployment snapshots queried 2–3 September 2026
supports: A bounded LIWO WFS query returns two primary and two regional candidates; point-in-polygon contains the two Wilhelminakanaal primary points and no regional candidate. Bbox-only records outside the polygon were not assigned.
Candidate points and frequency-class metadata are scenario-selection context, not active failures, forecasts, connected footprints, metre depths or safe-state evidence.

Seven cached observations are fresh for 2 September 2026. Marksluis reports 7 cm NAP below and 31 cm NAP above; Oosterhout Sluis 1 reports 514/513 cm NAP at adjacent points and exactly 0 m³/s at the spui/outlet around 17:20–17:30Z.

Timestamped observations require parameter, units, datum, issue/valid time and quality. An observed zero discharge is not perpetual no-flow or safety, and no Waterinfo forecast is assigned. Waterinfo is CC0/non-mission-critical; absent horizons remain NoData.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Climate-adaptation implementation agenda and detailed rain-stress evidence
evidenceSources.edition: Implementation agenda 2024–2026; stress-test studies 2019–2022 referenced by the municipality
supports: The municipality says the 2019 broad stress test did not always provide a sufficiently realistic picture and therefore commissioned deeper studies including paved surface and sewer behaviour.

Detailed studies cover Oosterheide's Bloemenbuurt, Schrijversbuurt, Natuurkundigenbuurt, Componistenbuurt and Warande, followed by Sterren-, Kastelen-, Kruiden- and Molenbuurt. The agenda identifies water-nuisance attention in Oosterheide and around Centrum.
A 70 mm rainfall design case identifies buildings at risk and potentially impassable roads. This is a static/design scenario with defined assumptions, not observed rain or a live depth map.

Weststad/Vijf Eiken received a quick scan and other neighbourhoods are planned for progressive assessment. Public PDF evidence does not supply a complete machine API, live sewer/groundwater/control state or explicit standard redistribution licence.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — 2026 drought, Marksluis and Mark–Vliet operational-control context
supports: On 4 August 2026 Rijkswaterstaat opened Marksluis at the water board's request to admit approximately 3–4 m³/s into Markkanaal/Mark–Vliet boezem for water quality during drought and blue-green algae pressure.

The 25 August notice at https://www.brabantsedelta.nl/actueel/nieuws/droogtemaatregelen-versoepeld/ says the restriction was lifted effective 26 August and Marksluis was no longer being used for extra flow because polder water was sufficient and demand declined.
The paired notices demonstrate a cross-authority controllable water-quality/drought pathway and its valid-time state; neither should be generalized to all future simulations.
Narrative operational notices are observed/action context, not a continuous licensed telemetry API or proof of all canal, polder, intake, pump, drinking-water or ecological states.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — Boswachterij Dorst, Vrachelse Heide and visitor/access context
evidenceSources.edition: Current visitor and municipal access pages inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Staatsbosbeheer describes Boswachterij Dorst as a roughly 1,000 ha forest/nature and year-round visitor area between Breda, Oosterhout and Tilburg, including Seterse Bergen and Vijf Eiken.

The municipal environmental vision identifies the southern forest zone, including Boswachterij Dorst, Landgoed Oosterheide and the Vrachelse/Teteringse/Seterse heaths, and notes concentrated recreation/access pressure near Ter Aalst.

The municipal access page at https://www.oosterhout.nl/bouwen-verbouwen-en-wonen/openbare-ruimte/natuurgebieden-betreden-met-voertuig-of-paard documents route/access controls in Vrachelse Heide and Boswachterij Dorst. Static restrictions do not establish incident access.

Official land-cover/visitor context establishes nature-fire eligibility and transient exposure only, not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, visitor count, extinguishing-water availability or suppression. No standard machine reuse licence was identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Oosterhout / Provincie Noord-Brabant / Omgevingsdienst Midden- en West-Brabant
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Weststad industrial/logistics exposure and hazardous-activity governance
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal and provincial pages inspected 3 September 2026; CBS 2025 business/building statistics
supports: The municipality describes Weststad I–III as approximately 350 ha in northwest Oosterhout along the A59 and Wilhelminakanaal, accessible by road, water and rail, with a 340 m quay and goods-transfer functions.

CBS 2025 records zero residents, 135 businesses and 122 non-residential buildings in Weststad-Zuid; Weststad-Noord has five residents, 80 businesses and 54 non-residential buildings. Vijf Eiken and Statendam add industrial exposure that resident-weighted allocation cannot represent.

The province's current hazardous-company page at https://www.brabant.nl/onderwerpen/veiligheid/omgevingsveiligheid-externe-veiligheid/risicovolle-bedrijven/ assigns Seveso/external-safety governance and points to the public risk map/OMWB. It does not itself identify an incident or current release in Oosterhout.

No event-valid workforce, visitor, freight, hazardous-inventory, plume, site emergency-plan or operating-state feed is consumed. Static business/building counts are exposure proxies, not occupancy or dangerous-substance quantities.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / Provincie Noord-Brabant / RIVM / OVapi / ProRail / Amphia
evidenceSources.title: E08 — A27/A59/N629, scheduled transit and external acute-care context
evidenceSources.edition: RWS notice published 1 September 2026; NWB-Light 1 August 2026; GTFS v9543 valid 30 August–12 December 2026; RIVM acute care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: NWB supplies eight logical links but five physical corridor identities: A59, A27, N629, N282 and N631. Paired A27/A59/N282 edges are series continuations, not additive emergency capacity, and all generalized route effects are Mobility/Supply-only.

Rijkswaterstaat announces September A27/A59 closures and an existing A27 Merwedebrug freight restriction; upcoming Hooipolder/A59 windows include connection closures and diversions. These are reference-date constraints, not perpetual closures, and the simulator assigns no current NDW situation.

The province's N629 page at https://www.brabant.nl/onderwerpen/verkeer-vervoer/wegen-infraprojecten-brabant/n629-oosterhout-dongen/ describes the Oosterhout–Dongen improvement project as under renewed discussion. Project status does not imply current road closure or capacity.

There is no ProRail passenger station in GM0826 and 52 GTFS stop areas include Oosterhout Busstation and Amphia Pasteurlaan. RIVM acute-care v1.1 (CC0) has no respondent point inside; nearest 24/7 surveyed acute site is Amphia Breda at 6.78 km centroid distance. Amphia's Oosterhout specialist location publishes weekday daytime hours, not 24/7 emergency care. Static geometry, schedules and survey status do not establish routes, passengers, ambulance time, acceptance, staffing or live operation.

HWH IMWA/DAMO is contributor-dependent/partial, weekly where supplied and CC BY-SA 4.0; register presence/type is not connected topology, telemetry, current operation, backup or restoration.

Brabant Water provides a location-specific drinking-water quality lookup, but public provider/quality context does not establish event-time source, zone, pressure, contamination, backup or restoration. Exact security-sensitive network topology remains unavailable/Unknown unless authorised.

One NBNL sample maps to Enexis OTD Oosteind and reports planning capacities/queues and nineteen projects with earliest year 2026. Planning/register points do not establish customers, live load/coverage, occupancy, shelter role or restoration.

VRMWB's current policy/planning page at https://www.vrmwb.nl/organisatie/beleid-en-planvorming establishes regional crisis governance, not activation or checkpoint performance. No complete public machine action/resource/decision feed or blanket licence was identified.

residualLimitations: This artifact audits a deterministic first-72-hour exercise model, not a forecast, warning, evacuation instruction, hydraulic assessment, road/transit operating decision, hospital status, industrial release assessment or operator restoration commitment.

CBS 2025 values are rounded/suppressed and residents exclude workers, freight users, commuters, pupils, patients/staff, nature visitors, transit passengers, responders and displaced people; no timestamped dynamic occupancy is consumed.

Generalized administrative polygons and centroids cannot resolve Wilhelminakanaal/Amertak/Donge/Mark hydraulics, outside-dike compartments, defence/control state, sewer/groundwater catchments, combustible vegetation, industrial sites or utility zones.

Two contained LIWO points are candidates, not breaches or footprints. Bbox queries include outside candidates unless polygon-filtered, and candidate metadata is not current probability, water level, depth or arrival.
Waterinfo observations are valid-time context and no local forecast is assigned. They are not selected as an exercise hydrograph; 0 m³/s at one outlet/time is not perpetual no-flow or safe state.
A future-standard WAD strengthening task and possible Amer system measure do not mean event-time failure. Design choice, temporary works and component condition remain Unknown without valid evidence.
Municipal stress studies establish planning/design cases, not a live rain event, groundwater field, sewer/pump/sluice state, completed measure or current local depth.

The controlled nature-fire source is synthetic. Official forest/visitor context does not establish fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, wind/plume, occupancy, access, extinguishing water, crew or suppression.
Weststad's area, business/building counts and logistics description do not establish current workforce, freight, hazardous inventory, release, plume or site operating/emergency state.

NWB, ProRail, GTFS and RWS planning notices are static/register/schedule/valid-time evidence. They do not establish continuous throughput, bus operation, passenger/freight demand, emergency priority or route performance.
Zero internal RIVM acute-care respondent points does not erase local care or demand. Distance to Amphia Breda is not route time, ambulance availability, acceptance, beds, staff, utilities or backup.

HWH coverage is partial/provider-dependent. Registered object, type or capacity does not establish connected topology, current operation, compatible flow units, power/backup, control sequence or recovery.

One NBNL sample, RDI antennas, DUO schools and absent local air/weather/NDW points are planning/register/coverage context. They do not establish customer connectivity, occupancy, load, signal, air surface, road state, reserve or repair.

Complete physical electricity, gas, drinking-water, wastewater, telecom, care, supply, transport and emergency-resource topology/live state may be unavailable or security-sensitive and remains Unknown or explicitly synthetic.

Exact hazard, neighbourhood, affected-population, service-availability, recovery and person-hour values remain synthetic/derived screening until critical/high findings are corrected and authorities review the selected event; impacts beyond T+72 are outside scope.
